# Exploratory from the shell: expl

expl calls the same operations the Exploratory MCP server offers. Exploratory Desktop must be running and
the user signed in.

## How to work

1. Find the command: `expl tools list --json` lists every command with its MCP tool name, whether it only
   reads, and its risk (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH).
2. Read its arguments before calling it: `expl <noun> <verb> --help` (same as `expl tools describe`).
3. Always pass `--json` and read the result from stdout. Warnings go to stderr: read them too.
4. Pass a project with `--project <id|name>`, or set one once with `expl project use <id|name>`.
5. Pass complex input as JSON: `--input file.json` or `--input -` (stdin). Flags override its fields.
6. HIGH-risk commands (publish, delete, ...) refuse to run without `--yes` when not on a terminal.
   Ask the user before you add `--yes`.
7. Long operations wait by default. With `--no-wait`, poll with `expl execution get <execution_id>`.
8. `expl call <tool_name>` runs a tool by its MCP name.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | The operation failed (NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PARAMETER, EXECUTION_FAILED, ...) |
| 2 | Usage error: unknown flag, unreadable JSON, or `--yes` missing |
| 3 | Exploratory Desktop is not running |
| 4 | Not signed in, unauthorized, or permission denied |
| 130 | Interrupted |

With `--json`, a failure prints `{"success": false, "error_code", "message", "suggested_actions"}` on stdout.
